text_blocks.snippet: A FERS retirement calculator estimates your federal pension annuity. The basic formula uses your High-3 average salary multiplied by your years of creditable service and a multiplier (typically 1% or 1.1%). The 1.1% multiplier applies if you retire at age 62 or later with 20 or more years of service. Serving Those Who Serve +2
You can calculate your estimated annuity by estimating how these three factors apply to you:

list.snippet: High-3 Salary: Your highest average basic pay earned during any 3 consecutive years of service. Capital Wealth +1
Creditable Service: Your total years and months of federal service. Unused sick leave also counts as additional time towards this total.

Multiplier: Usually 1.0%. This bumps to 1.1% if you are age 62 or older at the time of retirement with at least 20 years of service. Law enforcement officers, firefighters, and air traffic controllers use 1.7% for their first 20 years. Capital Wealth +2

text_blocks.snippet: Explore the following online options to receive a personalized estimate based on your specific age, service date, and salary:

list.snippet: FEDweek FERS & CSRS Calculator: Provides a quick, straightforward assessment of your potential annuity.
STWS FERS Retirement Calculator: Allows you to factor in specific retirement types (like regular, MRA+10, or VERA) and sick leave balances.
MyFEDBenefits MRA Calculator: Helps you identify your exact Minimum Retirement Age and your earliest eligible retirement date.

text_blocks.snippet: Disclaimer: Online calculators provide estimates for your educational planning. You should always obtain an official certified estimate from your agency's Human Resources department before submitting your retirement packet. www.myfeba.org
